I shortened the title of the dictation-v3 proposal, and `node Server/text-check.mjs` flagged nothing. The old title ran 31 words. The new one is "Web dictation V3: show replies and live words, pause the fast seat, merge read-aloud (you are a mastermind)".

I left the rest of the proposal alone. The owner asks are short bullets and the "Do" section is brief. I logged a "rewrote" line in `flags.jsonl`.

Two small things I did not change. `voice-assistant` and `audio/Recite` in the proposal are plain text rather than links. I also didn't screenshot it, since a proposal has no `page.js`.

I rewrote the `recite-voice` proposal in place for clarity. I edited only its `requirements.md` and did not run the owner-view screenshot check.

- **Title:** the old title was one 40-word line listing every feature. It is now "Read-aloud in the dictation chat, and a mic that ignores it". Under it, one line names the five pieces in build order, with links to Recite, Voice and Chat.
- **Step 4:** it was a single paragraph of about 170 words. It is now three bullets, covering the capture constraints, the echo drop, and where the logic lives.

`text-check` flagged nothing. I logged a "rewrote" line in `flags.jsonl`.

I wrote the review to `tap-unlock/review.md` with verdict `fix`; I didn't run it, so I haven't confirmed it plays on a phone.

The change does what `requirements.md` asks, but I found four problems:
- **Pause restarts the chunk:** if you pause mid-sentence and then tap Play, the first-tap unlock swaps the audio source for the silence clip. `resume()` then restarts the chunk from 0 instead of continuing.
- **Double fire:** one tap raises both `pointerdown` and `touchend`, and the "unlocked" flag only flips after the async `play()` resolves. The second event reassigns the source and calls `play()` again mid-flight.
- **Stale readme:** `Recite/readme.md` line 36 still describes the old behaviour.
- **No test and no task record:** nothing in `Recite.test.mjs` covers the refused-then-tap path. The task folder holds only `requirements.md` and `review/`, so there is no record of what was checked on a phone.

I also added two notes: the resume trigger depends on the error text containing "tap", and nothing in the task folder shows it working on a phone.

I wrote the review to `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/dictation-v3/recite-trace/review.md` with the verdict `fix`. I didn't run the code or open the Whisper log page, so the findings come from reading the diff and the surrounding files.

- **Settled replies leave no skip line (fix):** when auto is off, `final()` returns without logging anything. Only the streaming path writes "not read: auto is off", so a reply that arrives as a settled line can't be diagnosed from the log.
- **Docs not updated (fix):** the Recite readme and the Whisper readme and `doc/demo.md` don't mention the new `recite` lines or `trace()`.
- **Task folder too thin (fix):** it holds only `requirements.md`, so a fresh agent can't tell what was checked or whether the log page shows the new lines sensibly.
- **No "speak asked" line (note):** only the outcomes ("spoke", "speak failed") are logged, so a speak request that never returns leaves no trace.
- **Per-line `import()` (note):** `trace()` calls `import()` on every line, which is fine, and I found no simpler route.

I reviewed the dictation-v3 task: the verdict is **fix**. The review is in `dictation-v3/review.md`. I made no code edits.

**What works:**
- V3 now shows every reply, including the old-style `{chat}` lines. It also shows the reply while it is being written.
- Words already written are solid black at once. Gray is kept for the words not yet sent.
- One dropdown (`Chat V1 ▾`) replaces the v2/v3 chips, and V1 stays mounted underneath, so the mic keeps recording when you switch.
- The fast seat is off by default, and it has a test. A sentence ending in "?" still gets its Question, now filed by code.
- The smart seat is told to write replies that read well aloud.
- The karaoke playhead lights the sentence and word being read.
- The readmes changed in the same commits as the code.

**Four things must change:**
1. **Most read-aloud asks aren't built:**
   - the voice choice, speed and a Sample button in the dictation settings;
   - "switch your voice" by voice command;
   - the echo guard (the mic transcribed the read-aloud's own voice);
   - `voice-models.md` and the Kokoro RAM and CPU answer;
   - Chatterbox, and Servex running one voice engine with an idle shutdown.

   `plan.md` queues several of these, but the echo guard, voice sampling and the voice command aren't in its queue at all.
2. **`findings.md` §3 "What changed" is still a placeholder.** A fresh agent can't tell what landed on `worktree/dictation-v3` without it.
3. **Streaming replies only works for some sessions.** The session-id check in `ChatV3.wire()` uses `[w-]`, which matches only the letter "w" and "-". So only sessions whose id starts with `v-` get the live reply; it was probably meant to be `[\w-]`.
4. **One line in `Servex/agents/session-smart.md` is out of date.** Line 60 still says the fast assistant waits about 8 seconds, but the fast seat is now off.

**Smaller notes:**
- The Question ids use `Date.now()`, so two in the same millisecond would clash.
- The screenshots were taken before the link icon was removed, and none shows the new dropdown. Without them I could only check the requirements and the wording, not the page's layout.
- `Recite.Highlight` has no test.
- `fast-and-smart.md` now gives two statuses one line apart.

I rewrote step 1 of the v3-view proposal and left the rest as it was.

- **What was wrong:** Step 1 was one paragraph of about 130 words. The limit is 60.
- **The fix:** I split it into short bullets and made the proof line stand out. The file is `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/dictation-v3/v3-view/requirements.md`.
- **Nobody owns it:** I applied the rewrite myself and did not message an owner agent. I didn't check the agent list for one.
- **Script check:** `node Server/text-check.mjs` printed no flags on the folder.

I logged a "rewrote" line in `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl`.

I wrote the review to `sheet-reads/review.md` with verdict `fix`. The code looks like it does what the owner asked, but the docs and task folder fall short. I read the diff, the surrounding code and the readmes. I didn't run anything.

The three `[fix]` findings:
1. **Duplicated trace hook:** the same long `Recite.on_trace ??= …` line is pasted in both `Sheet.js` and `chat.js`, and the two regexes differ. Because of `??=`, only the first one that runs takes effect, so `chat.js`'s copy does nothing whenever a Sheet exists.
2. **Stale docs:** `audio/Recite/readme.md`, `ext/drawer/readme.md`, `ext/drawer/doc/sheet.md` and `ext/Chat/v2/readme.md` don't mention `on_trace`, `read_aloud()` or `report.diag`.
3. **Missing proof:** the task folder holds only `requirements.md` and the diff. There is no probe, shot or session-file excerpt behind the "proven headless" claim, so a fresh agent couldn't check it.

I also left three `[note]` items:
- The Sheet and `chat.js` now open two streams on the same session.
- The Sheet has none of `chat.js`'s `watching_since` guard.
- It's unclear whether `report.init` can safely run twice.

I wrote the review to `.../dictation-v3/join-and-follow/review.md` with verdict: fix. I checked the diff and requirements against the code. I did not run anything, so none of the four asks is confirmed working in practice.

The diff covers all four asks in code. The three `[fix]` findings are documentation gaps:

- **Link rule undocumented:** `ext/Chat` has no readme or doc line for `site_path()` or the same-tab link rule. Only `ux/Dictate/readme.md` documents the diff, and it covers asks 1 and 2 but not ask 4.
- **Sheet docs stale:** `ext/drawer/readme.md` and the Sheet docs don't describe the new session-following, the 5-second check or the read-aloud bar placement.
- **No verification record:** the task folder holds only `requirements.md` and the diff, with no trace lines or shots showing asks 1–3 working.

There are also five `[note]` items:

- **Two idle thresholds:** the join threshold is 30 minutes, but the Sheet's fallback follow hard-codes 2 hours.
- **Duplicated lookup:** the "latest voice session" lookup is written twice.
- **Uncleared interval:** the 5-second `setInterval` is never cleared.
- **`//` links:** a link starting with `//` is treated as a site path.
- **Silent resume failure:** a failed `Session.resume` in `ensure()` silently starts a new session with no trace line.

I wrote the review to `dictation-v3/v3-wall/review.md` with verdict `fix`: three [fix] items and four [note] items. I made no code edits and did not open the shot, so the 245 px claim is unchecked; I did not run the tests.

The change itself does what requirements.md asks. `prompt()` shows the AI text when there is one, otherwise the raw dictation split into paragraphs and clamped with "show all (N words)". The title falls back to a muted set of first words.

The three [fix] items:
1. **Stale readme:** line 99 of `ext/Chat/v3/readme.md` still says the card falls back to the live-written `paragraphs`, which the code no longer reads. It now contradicts the new bullet at line 100.
2. **Test weakened:** the live-append check in `ChatV3.test.mjs` was changed to wait for the raw "and more words" instead of the paragraph. I couldn't see any check for the new clamp, the "show all" toggle, the muted title or `ChatV3.paragraphs`, so those have no coverage.
3. **Task folder:** `v3-wall/` holds only `requirements.md`, with no `task.jsonl` and no pointer to the commit or to the shot as evidence, so a fresh agent couldn't continue from it alone.

The [note] items:
- An unrequested heading-size rule was added in `ChatV3.css`.
- A long AI `text` is not clamped.
- The first words show twice until the AI titles the card.
- `all_open` is created lazily instead of beside `raw_open`.

`voice-models.md` is written and sits beside `requirements.md` in your task folder. Only Kokoro was actually run. The VRAM and latency figures for the other models are secondary sources, and some cells say "not found".

- **Kokoro on this machine:** the model has about 1.26 GB resident (2.18 GB committed) and holds 1.27 GB during a render. Idle CPU is 0%. A render briefly uses about 16 of the 28 threads on the i7-14700K, roughly 59% of the CPU. A 21-word sentence rendered 7.2 s of audio in 1.16 s. The model files are 326 MB plus 28 MB of voices.
- **Why it runs on the CPU:** the server code never picks a device, and the venv has the CPU-only `onnxruntime`. A GPU would not improve the sound, because the model is the same. The "robotic" sound comes from the model's size.
- **Local recommendation:** try Chatterbox next. It fits in the free VRAM beside Whisper, is MIT-licensed, and has voice cloning and an emotion dial. Orpheus 3B is the alternative.
- **Cloud recommendation:** OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts, at about $0.70 an hour with a text field that steers tone. ElevenLabs is the alternative.
- **Claude app voice:** press reports say ElevenLabs, but I found no Anthropic statement, so the doc calls it "reported, unconfirmed".

I also wrote a copy into the worktree folder by mistake. The task dir lives in the main tree, so I copied the file there and logged a line in its `session.jsonl`. Nothing was committed, because the task dir isn't tracked in the worktree.

There is a mismatch, and I fixed it. The fix is committed on `worktree/dictation-active-session` (commit `04d651007`) and not merged, for you to review. The new headless test passes in the worktree. I did not run it against the unfixed code, so I haven't confirmed it fails there.

| Moment | Where the sentence goes | Where the view points | Where read-aloud listens |
|---|---|---|---|
| First open, no session | `chat.js:76` (`ensure`) joins the newest voice session if it spoke in the last 30 minutes, else starts one | Same session | `Sheet.js:78` applies the same rule |
| Switch session | The picked session (`resume_to`, `chat.js:118`) | Same | Same, through `on_change` |
| New session | None until the first sentence, which starts a new session (`fresh`) | Empty | **Mismatch:** it followed the old session (`Sheet.js:95`) |
| Reload | The id saved in `sessionStorage` | Same | Same |

There is never a moment with two active sessions. There is a moment with none only after New session, until the first sentence, and that is deliberate.

The mismatch: `Sheet.follow` didn't know New session had been pressed. So it fell back to the most recent session and read the old session's replies aloud. The fix is `chat.active()` in `chat.js`, which returns `{session, fresh}`. `Sheet.follow` now follows no session while `fresh` is set. I also bumped `READ_ALOUD_V` in `Sheet.js` to `2026-11-01e`.

The new test is `ux/Dictate/test/active-session.mjs`. It mocks Servex, covers all four moments, and asserts where each sentence is posted and which stream the Sheet opens. All checks pass. I ran `node --check` on the touched files. I also added the table as "The active session" in `ux/Dictate/doc/chat.md`, and the same table is logged on the task.

The verdict is **fix**: the change itself is correct, but three docs still say the fast seat is off by default. The report is at `dictation-v3/review.md`. Because the diff changes no page, it covers only Requirements and Words.

**What the diff does:** it sets the fast seat back to `voice` by default (commit 8a99d651c, worktree `fast-seat-voice`).
- That follows the owner's later word, which I checked in the session's `session.jsonl`, Prompt `qrct21sx`: "turning it off isn't going to fix anything".
- With the seat on, code no longer files a Question for each "?" sentence; it only does that when the seat is off. So the seat and code never both file one.
- `Sessions.test.mjs` passes its 28 checks.
- It takes effect at the next Servex restart, which must not happen during a voice call.

**Must change:**
1. `Servex/agents/session-smart.md:19` is the smart seat's own prompt, and it still says "there is usually no fast assistant". The live smart seat will act as the only voice while the voice assistant works beside it.
2. `findings.md:44` and its §2 still say the fast seat is off by default, and never mention that the owner reversed it. A fresh agent reading only this task folder would think the pause still stands.

**Worth a look:**
3. A comment in `Widget.css:254` says that with the seat off, nothing "settles", which is why the old fade was dropped. With the seat back on, the fade may need to come back.
4. `fast-and-smart.md:3` says the seat "does half of the work"; the owner said it "might be". It should quote the owner and link the prompt.

I made no code edits.

I made all three of the reviewer's fixes. They're committed as `f3f491d03` on `worktree/dictation-active-session` and not merged, so the parent can merge. The test still passes with all 11 checks, and `node --check` is clean on `Sheet.js`.

- **One function:** the Sheet now takes the session from `chat.active().session` in all three places it used `chat.current()`, not just the `fresh` flag. The send and the view still read the controller's state directly, so the doc now says that plainly instead of claiming all three call the function.
- **`ext/drawer/readme.md:34`:** it now says read-aloud follows no session after New session, until the first sentence starts one.
- **`ux/Dictate/readme.md`:** `test/active-session.mjs` is listed with the other tests.
- **First open before the first sentence:** I added this moment to the doc table. Read-aloud may already follow the recent session while the view is still empty. I left this as it is, because the first sentence joins that same session.
- **Line numbers:** added to the table rows in `doc/chat.md`.

The task still needs landing once it is merged.

The fix doesn't work yet: it would never clear the cache on a phone that already has the page cached. The review is written to `dictation-v3/review.md` with `verdict: fix`.

The change is the site gateway's stale-file fix, still only on `worktree/gateway-cache` (commit b2d5ab853). It's meant to stop a phone running an old `Sheet.js` over monorepo.lew42.com. Both tests pass in the worktree: `SiteGateway.cache.test.mjs` passes all 5 checks and `SiteGateway.test.mjs` is ok.

**Fixes needed:**
1. **The cache clear never happens on a phone.** The gateway only sends the clear on a full page reply (a 200). On a repeat load, the real site sends a 304 "not modified" (`Server/Server.js:43`, `Server/compress.js:92`), so the phone keeps its old `Sheet.js`. A simple fix: for a browser that hasn't been cleared yet, the gateway's `headers()` (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:103`) strips the "do I have the latest?" headers from page loads, so the site has to send a 200.
2. **The test can't catch fix 1.** Its fake site always sends a 200 and never a 304, unlike the real site.
3. **The task folder doesn't record this work.** `findings.md` doesn't mention it, and there's no sub-folder or log line for it. A fresh agent reading `dictation-v3/` alone wouldn't know the fix exists or that it serves the first priority: read-aloud over monorepo.lew42.com.

**Notes:**
- The new default of "always check with the site" changes little for static files, which have sent it since 2026-10-05. It still covers other routes, so it's harmless.
- Chrome can pause a page load briefly while it clears the cache. That happens once per browser, but the doc should say so, so a slow first load isn't mistaken for a new bug.

The diff changes no page, so the review covers only Requirements and Words, with no screenshots.

Report delivered to `mastermind-dictation-v3`. Summary: V1 and V3 both pass the dim-to-strong ink check (guess at `--draft-ink` 70% alpha, sent at `--final-ink` solid); V2 has no guess element at all, by design, so there's nothing to check there — flagged as a possible gap, not a fail.
